title: From transition counts to a bigram model
description: A quick reference for the count-table, probability-row, and smoothing terms used here.

terms.definition: A next-token model whose prediction depends only on the current token.
The number of times one token immediately precedes another in the training documents.
The preceding information used to condition a prediction; a bigram keeps one token.
One normalized table row giving next-token probabilities for a selected current token.
The probability estimate obtained by dividing observed counts by a positive row total.
A candidate next token with zero count after an otherwise observed context.
A current token with no observed outgoing transitions, leaving its MLE row undefined.
A rule that adds one pseudocount to every candidate before row normalization.
An artificial positive count added to observed counts by a smoothing rule.
